title: Anthrobots form three morphotypes, split first by size and shape, then by cilia pattern

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Anthrobots form three morphotypes, split first by size and shape, then by cilia pattern

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Principal component analysis and clustering of eight shape and cilia indices from about 350 Anthrobots yields three morphotypes, organized as a decision tree in which size and shape smoothness separate small, smooth spherical bots (morphotype 1) from larger, irregular bots, which are then split by cilia pattern into non-polarized (morphotype 2) and polarized (morphotype 3).

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Distinct Morphological Types

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In summary, our morphological characterization pipeline suggest that Anthrobots self‐organize into 3 major morphotypes (Figure 3E) and this relationship can be represented by a developmental decision tree shown on Figure 3F wherein the first “decision point” determines the Anthrobot size and shape.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Gumuskaya G, Srivastava P, Cooper BG, Lesser H, Semegran B, Garnier S, Levin M, “Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells”, Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) (2024), doi:10.1002/advs.202303575; section “Results › Anthrobots Self‐Organize into Distinct Morphological Types”. Scope: About 350 NHBE-derived Anthrobots imaged by confocal microscopy

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-anthrobots-13: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.69

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The statistical cluster claim is reproducible in principle with explicit features and methods. The developmental-tree interpretation and incomplete public raw stacks make only part of the claim resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Apply PCA and competing clustering methods to the eight indices, evaluate support for three clusters, and test whether the proposed size/shape-then-cilia tree predicts held-out assignments.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A decision tree over final measurements is not direct evidence of developmental decisions.

Three-cluster support may depend on scaling and algorithm choice.

fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.76
discriminating power: 0.62
data existence: 0.62

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The morphotype tree is a clustering claim about a defined feature set of about 350 bots. That matrix is not deposited, and cluster count is method-dependent even when the matrix exists. Open figures do not let a third party rerun the principal components or test whether three groups are preferred.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Repeat principal-component analysis and clustering on the eight shape and cilia indices, and compare a three-group solution with two- and four-group solutions by a pre-specified criterion. A stable split of small smooth spheres from larger irregular bots, and a further cilia-pattern split of the large bots, would support the decision tree; a continuum or a different first split would refute three morphotypes in that order.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Size and shape are partly the same measurement, so the first split can be a size threshold.

Three clusters and a tree order are sensitive to scaling and to the choice of k.

The eight-index matrix is not public.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data existence: 0.16
discriminating power: 0.4
data adequacy: 0.16
operationalizability: 0.78
